reason: Subsection 18(2) bars entry on the register unless authorized by the Act or by-laws and supported by evidence satisfying the Registrar that the person is entitled.

proposedGroups.title: Evidence required before entry on register
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 18(2) bars entry on the register unless authorized by the Act or by-laws and supported by evidence satisfying the Registrar that the person is entitled.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the authorization and evidence requirements before a name can be entered in the register.

reason: Subsection 18(3) allows a person affected by a Registrar registration decision to appeal to Council, which may reconsider and order entry of the person's name.

proposedGroups.title: Appeal from Registrar registration decisions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 18(3) allows a person affected by a Registrar registration decision to appeal to Council, which may reconsider and order entry of the person's name.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand the Council appeal route for registration decisions made by the Registrar.

reason: Subsection 18(4) requires the Registrar each year to print, publish, and keep for free office inspection an alphabetical list with addresses of persons registered as of February 1.

proposedGroups.title: Annual published list of registrants
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 18(4) requires the Registrar each year to print, publish, and keep for free office inspection an alphabetical list with addresses of persons registered as of February 1.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the annual publication and inspection duty for the list of registered land surveyors.

reason: Subsection 18(5) makes the register or annual list prima facie court evidence of registration and allows Registrar certification for names not appearing on the list.

proposedGroups.title: Register and list as evidence of registration
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 18(5) makes the register or annual list prima facie court evidence of registration and allows Registrar certification for names not appearing on the list.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand how the register, annual list, and Registrar certificates prove registration status.

reason: Subsection 19(1) requires each member to pay annual Association fees fixed by by-law on or before February 1 each year.

proposedGroups.title: Annual fee payment deadline
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(1) requires each member to pay annual Association fees fixed by by-law on or before February 1 each year.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the annual fee deadline for Association members.

reason: Subsection 19(2) provides that, subject to late-payment relief, a member who fails to pay annual fees loses Act rights and privileges and is not placed on the register.

proposedGroups.title: Consequences of unpaid annual fees
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(2) provides that, subject to late-payment relief, a member who fails to pay annual fees loses Act rights and privileges and is not placed on the register.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand what happens to member rights, privileges, and register status after nonpayment of annual fees.

reason: Subsection 19(3) allows a person who missed the annual fee deadline to pay in full within one year, after which the person's name may be added to the register effective only from payment.

proposedGroups.title: Late payment within one year
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(3) allows a person who missed the annual fee deadline to pay in full within one year, after which the person's name may be added to the register effective only from payment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the one-year late-payment route back onto the register and its effective date.

reason: Subsection 19(4) requires Council approval after the one-year late-payment route expires and lets Council require fees, examinations, or other public-interest conditions before adding the name to the register.

proposedGroups.title: Reinstatement after extended fee default
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 19(4) requires Council approval after the one-year late-payment route expires and lets Council require fees, examinations, or other public-interest conditions before adding the name to the register.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand Council's options when a former member seeks registration after failing to pay within one year.

reason: Subsection 20(1) creates a Complaints Committee consisting of a Council member as chair and two other Association members appointed by Council.

proposedGroups.title: Complaints Committee composition
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(1) creates a Complaints Committee consisting of a Council member as chair and two other Association members appointed by Council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the required composition of the Complaints Committee.

reason: Subsection 20(2) requires Council to name two alternate Complaints Committee members who may be called on by the chair as necessary.

proposedGroups.title: Alternate Complaints Committee members
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(2) requires Council to name two alternate Complaints Committee members who may be called on by the chair as necessary.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand how alternate Complaints Committee members are provided.

reason: Subsection 20(3) bars a member of the Discipline Committee from also serving on the Complaints Committee.

proposedGroups.title: Separation of complaints and discipline committees
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(3) bars a member of the Discipline Committee from also serving on the Complaints Committee.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the membership separation rule between complaints and discipline bodies.

reason: Subsection 20(4) sets three Complaints Committee members as quorum.

proposedGroups.title: Complaints Committee quorum
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 20(4) sets three Complaints Committee members as quorum.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the quorum number for Complaints Committee business.

reason: Subsection 21(1) requires the Complaints Committee to consider and investigate public or member complaints, but bars action unless a written complaint was filed, the member was notified and given at least two weeks to respond, and records were examined or reasonably sought.

proposedGroups.title: Complaint investigation prerequisites
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 21(1) requires the Complaints Committee to consider and investigate public or member complaints, but bars action unless a written complaint was filed, the member was notified and given at least two weeks to respond, and records were examined or reasonably sought.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand the notice, response, and records-review prerequisites before the Complaints Committee acts on a complaint.

reason: Subsection 21(2) allows the Complaints Committee to refer all or part of a matter to the Discipline Committee, decline referral, or take appropriate non-inconsistent action to resolve the complaint.

proposedGroups.title: Complaints Committee disposition options
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 21(2) allows the Complaints Committee to refer all or part of a matter to the Discipline Committee, decline referral, or take appropriate non-inconsistent action to resolve the complaint.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the possible outcomes after the Complaints Committee reviews complaint information.

reason: Subsection 21(3) requires the Complaints Committee to give its written decision and reasons to the Registrar for the purposes of delivery under subsection 21(4).

proposedGroups.title: Written complaint decision and reasons
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 21(3) requires the Complaints Committee to give its written decision and reasons to the Registrar for the purposes of delivery under subsection 21(4).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the written-decision and reasons step after the Complaints Committee decides a complaint.

reason: Subsection 21(4) requires the Registrar to deliver or mail the Complaints Committee's written decision and reasons to the complainant and the person complained against.

proposedGroups.title: Delivery of complaint decision to parties
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 21(4) requires the Registrar to deliver or mail the Complaints Committee's written decision and reasons to the complainant and the person complained against.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Understand who receives the complaint decision and how the Registrar sends it.

reason: Subsection 21(5) allows a dissatisfied complainant to apply to Council for review of the complaint's treatment, which Council may refer under subsection 22(6).

proposedGroups.title: Council review requested by dissatisfied complainant
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 21(5) allows a dissatisfied complainant to apply to Council for review of the complaint's treatment, which Council may refer under subsection 22(6).
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the complainant review route after dissatisfaction with the Complaints Committee disposition.

reason: Subsection 22(1) creates a Discipline Committee of five persons appointed by Council.

proposedGroups.title: Discipline Committee composition
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 22(1) creates a Discipline Committee of five persons appointed by Council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Know the appointment authority and size of the Discipline Committee.
